subject: Annual commit tiers — Starter / Growth / Enterprise + surge protection proposal
messages:

Subject: Annual commit tiers — Starter / Growth / Enterprise + surge protection proposal

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for taking time last week. Based on the usage profile you shared (80% search queries, average request length ~45 tokens, heavy daytime peaks), I put together a compact annual-commit proposal that aims to balance predictable unit economics with short-term burst protection during Black Friday-style spikes.

High level (attached: BR-commit-matrix-v2.xlsx):
- Starter: 0.5M tokens/month (6M annual) — intended for limited pilot teams; 5% off list per-token rate, no burst allowance beyond committed slab.
- Growth: 3M tokens/month (36M annual) — recommended for product rollouts; 18% off list + 20% monthly surge pool (consumable credits).
- Enterprise: 10M tokens/month (120M annual) — full production with predictable throughput; 28% off list, 40% surge pool, and SLA-backed latency tiers.

Key design decisions:
- Surge protection: We model a temporary burst pool (percentage of monthly commit) that consumes credits before overage costs apply. This avoids large overage bills on short peaks.
- Carryover: Unused commit in Starter and Growth can carry up to one month only; Enterprise allows two-month carryover.
- Pricing floor: All offers assume 12-month payment term with monthly reporting; upfront payment unlocks an additional 3% credit.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm which teams you want scoped into the Growth tier vs Starter by May 6.
2) We can bake the SOW language (attached: SOW_draft_BrightRetail_v1.pdf) to capture surge pool mechanics.
3) If procurement needs a single-line PO-friendly price, I can push a one-page summary for legal.

Two quick notes for our side: looping Marissa for approval of the 28% lid on Enterprise pricing, and Soojin for SOW language on data retention.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few clarifying questions from our side after a first pass:
1) For the Growth surge pool (20%), is that a one-time monthly buffer or rolled into a credit bank? How does expiration work?
2) On overage rates: can you confirm the per-token overage price once the surge pool is exhausted (and whether the price scales with the tier)?
3) For Enterprise SLA: are there regional latency targets (we run primarily in us-east and eu-west)?

Procurement also asked whether you can provide an example invoice line that shows how the surge credits would appear.

Looking forward — we have a billing review on Thursday and would like to bring a draft to that meeting.

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commit tiers — Starter / Growth / Enterprise + surge protection proposal

Alex —

Answers inline:
1) Growth surge pool mechanics: the 20% is an explicit monthly buffer — credits are consumed first and expire at month-end (designed to protect against short peaks within the billing cycle). Enterprise pool (40%) rolls into a 2-month credit buffer to smooth multi-week campaigns.
2) Overage rates: Starter overage = list price + 40%; Growth overage = list price + 20%; Enterprise overage = list price + 10%. The idea is to keep Enterprise overage meaningful but not punitive. We can supply a sample invoice line that shows: committed tokens, surge credits consumed, overage tokens, and effective blended per-token price. I'll attach an invoice mock in the next email.
3) Regional SLAs: yes — Enterprise includes region-aware latency targets (us-east p95 < 120ms; eu-west p95 < 160ms). We guarantee failover to a secondary region for critical routes; details in SOW.

Procurement example: see attached invoice-mock-20270420.xlsx (I will upload to Drive link next).

If these are acceptable, Marissa can confirm the final discount cap on Enterprise (we penciled 28% but have internal room to 30% with a 24-month commit).

Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
